The geographic area includes the coastal area in Golden Bay (Maltese: Il-Mixquqa) to Il-Prajjet and Ix- Xagħra l-Ħamra. It was declared a national park in  the Malta Government Gazette by Legal Notice 251 of 2007 in September 2007. The park is named for the northwestern region or wind (Maltese: Majjistral).
The area includes a stretch of 6 kilometres (3.7 mi) of protected coast, designated as part of a larger Special Area of Conservation of International Importance, within the Natura 2000 network of sites as per the European Habitats Directive. It has a number of historic and archaeological sites as identified in studies commissioned by the Malta Tourism Authority. 


== Habitats ==
The Maltese Islands have a variety of habitats that are inhabited by diverse wild native plants. Some plants in the park are also endemic (found only in the Maltese islands), sub-endemic (found also in a few other Mediterranean regions), while others are scarce, localised or rare. While strolling in the Majjistral Park it is possible to observe the local environment, represented by a wide range of plants found in the different habitats...","coordinates":[{"lat":35.946,"lon":14.339,"primary":true,"globe":"earth"}],"pageimage":"Majjistral-Nature-and-History-Park.jpg","pageprops":{"page_image_free":"Majjistral-Nature-and-History-Park.jpg","wikibase-shortdesc":"Nature reserve in Mellieha, Malta","wikibase_item":"Q96391580"}}]}}
